title: Investment case for telemetry tiering and compact signal set
summary: A concise investment case proposing a three-tier telemetry model and a compact signal set for inference services to reduce query cost, simplify dashboards, and keep SLI coverage intact. Includes rough cost estimates, sampling heuristics, dashboard pruning plan, and rollout checklist.
outline: Problem statement: telemetry cost growth + operator overload
Proposed solution: three telemetry tiers + compact signal set
SLO-to-signal mapping and minimal signal catalog
Sampling & retention heuristics for traces and spans
Estimated cost impact and ROI timeline
decisions: Adopt a 3-tier telemetry model (Tier A: SLO-critical, Tier B: high-value diagnostics, Tier C: ephemeral/debug)
Enforce a compact signal set (<= 18 primary signals across inference runtime) for operator-facing dashboards
Apply feature-flagged adaptive trace sampling with severity-weighted retention (80% of budget to Tier A traces)
Introduce a quarterly telemetry audit to prune low-usage widgets and query-heavy panels
sli_mapping: SLO: 99.9% p99 latency - Signals: request_latency.{p50,p90,p99}, cold_start_rate, kv_cache_hit_ratio
SLO: error_rate < 0.1% - Signals: server_error_count, model_fallback_count, rate_limit_exceeded_count
SLO: throughput guarantee (requests/sec) - Signals: serving_capacity_utilization, queue_length_95
Quality SLO (botched generations) - Signals: model_rollout_error_rate, postprocess_failures
sampling_plan: Tiering: label traces/spans at ingest as TierA|TierB|TierC based on route, token count, SLO impact
TierA (SLO-critical): keep 100% of spans for 7d, full trace retention for 30d for high-severity events
TierB (diagnostic): adaptive sampling 10-20% baseline, increase to 100% on anomaly or during rollout windows
TierC (debug/experimental): aggressive reservoir sampling (1-2%); drop high-cardinality attributes unless flagged
Severity weighting: traces with error tags or fallback flags promoted to higher retention automatically
Prefix/KV caching: instrument sample keys to capture cache-miss traces at higher rates
Trace size cap: truncate spans beyond 1k spans and emit a summary span to control storage
dashboard_pruning_rules: Rule 1: Panels must map to >=1 SLO or operator incident playbook within 90 days
Rule 2: Panels with >5x query cost vs actionable value get archived to a 'deep-dive' dashboard
Rule 3: No dashboard should include more than 3 high-cardinality filters by default
Rule 4: Schedule low-frequency reports (daily/weekly) for heavy queries instead of live panels
Rule 5: Use pre-aggregated rollup views for token/latency distributions where possible
cost_estimates_and_roi: Baseline telemetry spend (hosted tracing + metrics + logs): $120k/mo (current estimate across prod regions)
Projection after first rollout (tiering + sampling): expected 30-45% reduction in storage/query cost -> $66k-$84k/mo
Engineering effort: ~3.5 FTE-months (implement sampling, tagging, dashboard migration)
Payback window: 3-6 months based on cost reduction and reduced oncall overhead
Soft benefits: faster incident triage (reduce MTTI by estimated 10-20%), fewer noisy alerts
implementation_todo: 1) Define TierA/TierB/TierC routing rules by team and route (matrix to be completed)
2) Add trace-level 'telemetry_tier' tag at edge and in SDKs
3) Implement adaptive sampler in tracing pipeline and haze tests in staging
4) Create compact signal dashboards and a 'deep-dive' archive space
5) Add guardrails to pre-commit Lint (prevent new high-cardinality fields without approval)
6) Run 6-week pilot on two high-traffic models and one low-traffic model
7) Audit existing dashboards and mark candidates for pruning before rollout
rollout_checklist: Pilot start (week 0): enable Tier tags in staging; baseline metrics capture
Pilot week 2: enable TierA full retention for pilot routes; monitor query cost delta
Pilot week 4: evaluate operator workflows and refine signal set
Pilot week 6: decision gate (go/no-go) based on cost reduction >=20% and no SLO regressions
Phase 1 (prod initial): roll TierA on all SLO-critical routes, TierB sampling at 20%
Phase 2 (complete): onboard remaining routes, enforce dashboard pruning rules
Post-rollout (quarterly): telemetry audit and signal churn review
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Under-sampling hides rare failure modes -> Mitigation: severity promotion + scheduled 100% retention windows for rollouts
Risk: Operator confusion with new dashboard layout -> Mitigation: 2-week operator training + migration guide
Risk: Hidden cost of pre-aggregation -> Mitigation: estimate compute vs storage trade-offs in pilot and measure query latency
Risk: Missing high-cardinality attributes for debugging -> Mitigation: maintain a short 'debug capture' flag developers can toggle per-release
success_metrics: Telem spend reduction >= 25% within 3 months of rollout
No regression in SLO detection or mean time to detect (MTTD) beyond 10%
Reduction in noisy dashboard panels by >= 60% (archived or converted to scheduled reports)
notes:
Context and rationale:

Telemetry costs have been trending up with model variety and per-tenant instrumentation. Operators report too many panels and slow investigative queries. This doc lays out an investment-case style proposal: small upfront engineering effort to introduce a tiering model and compact signal set that retains SLO coverage but reduces storage and query charges.

Unique points in this proposal:
- Treat telemetry as product-level budget with explicit ROI expectations (not just an infra checkbox).
- Prioritize SLO fidelity and operator workflows over raw signal volume.
- Use adaptive, severity-weighted sampling rather than blunt reservoir sampling.

Open questions (for working group):
